decisions.title: Fix route

options.label: Layered: prevention guard + detection/refuse net, investigation-first
options.consequence: SC1 rests on prevention with the detection net as a bounded backstop; two small subsystems ship instead of one, and the mechanism must be pinned empirically before the guard is trusted.

options.label: Prevention-only (guard connection)
options.consequence: If the guard leaks (mechanism other than a lock window, or silent guard death), silent data loss returns and SC2 has no implementation.

options.label: Detection + recovery only
options.consequence: Every mid-flow CLI read rides the loss window until detection fires; durability then depends on salvage checkpointing working on an unlinked inode.

decisions.rationale: US2 contracts a named event and refusal in every path, which prevention-only cannot provide; SC1 contracts durability, which detection-only cannot guarantee. The layered route is the smallest one satisfying both.

decisions.title: Detection home

options.label: Revive and extend the dead WalMonitor; wire its spawn at node startup
options.consequence: One background task owns WAL health (size, checkpoint, integrity); existing checkpoint machinery is reused; the currently-unspawned monitor (probe A3) becomes live code.

options.label: New standalone integrity watchdog module
options.consequence: A second periodic task duplicates the tick, pool access, and checkpoint plumbing the monitor already has.

options.label: Per-write detection hook in the DB layer
options.consequence: Hot-path cost on every write and no coverage while the node is idle — which is when the incident occurred.

decisions.rationale: The monitor exists, is shaped for this, and is dead only for want of a spawn site; extending it is the smallest live home.

decisions.title: Salvage strategy on detected unlink

options.label: Checkpoint via open file descriptors, then refuse writes (stay up)
options.consequence: Committed frames are flushed to the main DB through the surviving connections' fds if A6 holds; the node then holds an exclusive lock so writes fail loudly while reads continue; no in-place heal is claimed.

options.label: Hardlink the unlinked WAL back via /proc/self/fd
options.consequence: Probe-refuted at /wai:spec: linkat(AT_SYMLINK_FOLLOW) on a proc-fd symlink of a deleted file fails with ENOENT on the target host, so the path cannot be restored in place.

options.label: Byte copy-back of the orphaned WAL to its path
options.consequence: A new inode at the path does not heal the split between old-fd connections and new connections; the bytes become a forensic artifact, not recovery.

decisions.rationale: The only option whose data-saving half (checkpoint via fd) is verifiable in T1 and whose failure half still satisfies US2 (named event + refusal).

decisions.title: Prevention mechanism

options.label: Dedicated wal-index-holding guard connection
options.consequence: One long-lived connection keeps the wal-index mapped so an external close can never become the last locker able to checkpoint+unlink; adoption is gated on T1 proving it blocks the unlink on the real node, with DP2 as the authorised halt if refuted.

options.label: Set SQLITE_FCNTL_PERSIST_WAL on node connections
options.consequence: The flag governs the closing behavior of the node's own connections only; the unlinking close belongs to the external CLI, which cannot be flagged.

options.label: Filesystem permissions on the WAL file
options.consequence: The node itself must create, write, and checkpoint the WAL as the same UID; permission games break normal operation or are trivially bypassed.

decisions.rationale: The incident occurred while min_connections=2 pool connections were alive, showing pooled connections do not reliably hold the wal-index lock; an explicit guard whose only job is holding it is the smallest deterministic prevention.

decisions.title: verify_cmd packaging

options.label: One script, two legs: scripts/live/wal-unlink-durability-repro.sh
options.consequence: A single verify_cmd covers the guard-on durability leg (SC1) and the guard-off detection/refusal leg (SC2) plus the SC3 captures.

decisions.single_option_reason: SC4 contracts exactly one verify_cmd, and the two legs are one flow with an env flag flipped; one script with two legs is the minimal faithful form — any second option would be an invented alternative.
decisions.rationale: Single-script packaging keeps the ship-flow verify step deterministic.

options.label: Refuse writes, stay up
options.consequence: Writes fail fast and loudly while reads and the management API stay available for diagnosis; remediation is an operator restart named in the ERROR event.

options.label: Checkpoint then exit for supervisor restart
options.consequence: Availability depends on a supervisor existing; manually started nodes go DOWN instead of degraded — worse for exactly the unattended deployments this bug bites.

options.label: In-place pool recycle
options.consequence: DBService.pool is shared via Arc across the server; a hot swap risks dangling old connections re-creating the split world it exists to end.

obstacles.obstacle: The guard premise fails on the real binary — the unlink mechanism turns out not to be a wal-index lock window (the single-process model did not reproduce, so the real mechanism is still unproven).
obstacles.countermeasure: T1 instrumented investigation on the real node gates D4; DP2 is the authorised halt if the guard is refuted; the detection net still bounds loss to the detection window.

obstacles.obstacle: The salvage checkpoint cannot flush frames from an unlinked WAL (A6 unproven), so writes committed between unlink and trip are lost even with the net.
obstacles.countermeasure: T1 includes a validation leg proving or disproving checkpoint-via-open-fd on the real binary; if refuted, the loss is still NAMED (wal_salvage_checkpoint_failed + refusal) per US2, never silent.

obstacles.obstacle: The event fires but is unnamed or unactionable, failing the 'named, actionable' contract.
obstacles.countermeasure: Fixed event strings (wal_unlinked_externally, wal_write_refusal_active) carrying DB path and remediation text; the guard-off repro leg asserts the exact log line.

obstacles.obstacle: The monitor is never spawned — WalMonitor is dead code today (probe A3), so 'extend the monitor' alone ships nothing.
obstacles.countermeasure: The workstream wires WalMonitor::spawn_default into node startup; a startup INFO log line is asserted in the repro so a missing spawn cannot go green silently.

obstacles.obstacle: The guard connection, inotify watch, and refusal machinery add measurable write-path cost.
obstacles.countermeasure: Guard is one idle connection, the watch is one directory fd, and the trip latch is untouched when untripped; TS4 captures pre/post write-path timings into the decisions-ledger baseline SC3 names.

obstacles.obstacle: The fix accidentally changes the journal mode or checkpoint cadence.
obstacles.countermeasure: The repro asserts PRAGMA journal_mode = wal offline after the run; existing wal_monitor checkpoint intervals are unchanged.

obstacles.obstacle: Repro flakiness: the unlink depends on the node's lock state at CLI close, so a naive script passes/fails nondeterministically.
obstacles.countermeasure: The script polls /proc for the wal-deleted fd state (and retries the CLI-read step on a fresh scratch DB) rather than assuming the unlink landed; the red leg on current code is verified as part of T1.

obstacles.obstacle: Scratch-node port or state collisions with other sessions (the :9012 pattern is shared).
obstacles.countermeasure: Preflight port check plus a fresh mktemp scratch dir per run; cleanup trap kills only the spawned PID (no pkill, per the safe-process rule).

obstacles.obstacle: The guard connection dies silently (pool recycle, transient error) and prevention is silently off while everything looks green.
obstacles.countermeasure: The monitor health-checks the guard each tick and re-establishes it with a named WARN (wal_guard_reconnected); a guard that cannot be re-established escalates to the same trip path as an unlink.

decision_points.trigger: T1 evidence shows the backup subsystem shares the unlink hazard, crossing this spec's out-of-scope boundary; continuing requires scope renegotiation with the operator, not silent scope growth.

T1 refutes the guard-connection prevention (an external close still unlinks the WAL while the guard holds the wal-index lock), so D4 cannot be adopted as designed and the route must be re-settled with the operator.

assumptions.claim: Deployment and dev hosts are Linux with inotify and /proc/self available.
assumptions.probe: uname -s → Linux; test -d /proc/self/fd succeeded (2026-08-28, this host).

assumptions.claim: A sqlite3 CLI is available on hosts where the reproduction runs.
assumptions.probe: sqlite3 t.sqlite 'select count(*) from items;' executed successfully in the 2026-08-28 mechanism experiment.

assumptions.claim: WalMonitor (crates/db/src/wal_monitor.rs) has no spawn site in the workspace; detection requires wiring one at node startup.
assumptions.probe: Repo-wide grep for WalMonitor::spawn / spawn_default call sites (2026-08-28): only the definition and lib.rs re-export exist.

assumptions.claim: Node pools run min_connections=2, idle_timeout=600s, WAL mode, synchronous=NORMAL (crates/db/src/lib.rs:46-52 and 392-407), so pooled connections alone did not prevent the incident.
assumptions.probe: Read of crates/db/src/lib.rs constant definitions and pool builders.

assumptions.claim: A live connection holding the WAL wal-index blocks an external close from unlinking the WAL; the guard premise must be revalidated against the real node binary in T1.
assumptions.probe: Python WAL-mode experiment (2026-08-28): CLI close left the WAL intact while a WAL-mode connection was open.

assumptions.claim: PRAGMA wal_checkpoint issued on a surviving connection flushes frames held in an unlinked WAL inode into the main DB; if false, salvage reduces to a named failure plus refusal and US2 is still satisfied.
assumptions.probe: T1 validation leg on the real :9012 scratch node (cannot be probed before the instrumented reproduction exists).

questions.asked: When the detection safety net fires (external unlink detected despite the prevention guard), what should the node do after attempting the checkpoint-via-open-fd salvage: refuse writes and stay up; checkpoint then exit for supervisor restart; or attempt an in-place pool recycle?
